voice_clone.note: Zero-shot clone. The adapter truncates the reference to 10 s (ref_audio_max_duration_s) and supplies a placeholder transcript when the voice library has none. Not required on its own: voice_design alone is a valid request.

voice_design.note: Natural-language voice traits (gender / accent / age / whisper), passed to the engine as instruct. Combines with voice_clone to steer a cloned delivery.

duration_s.note: Optional. Omitted, the engine's RuleDurationEstimator picks the length; supplied, it commits ceil(duration_s * 25) latent frames up front.

speed.note: OmniVoice.generate() accepts no speed argument, so this is one FFmpeg tempo pass on the finished WAV rather than an engine parameter.

non_verbal_tags.note: The engine's own atomic tag set. Any other bracketed word — [cough], [breath], [gasp] — is not a tag: it falls through to ordinary tokenization and renders as noise.

hardware.note: 8 GB completes without swapping but leaves under 1 GB free at warning pressure; suited to a dedicated fleet worker, not a machine in general use.

section_budget_quality_gate.method: transcribe-back word coverage, same text/seed/voice, only the section budget varying
section_budget_quality_gate.mechanism: OmniVoice commits target_len frames up front from its duration estimator and must fill exactly that budget; over a long span the estimate drifts long and the surplus becomes silence and dropped words, not extra pauses.

memory_qualification.method: 3 reps per tier, escalating duration through each machine's own job engine

engine_findings: OmniVoice.generate() accepts no speed argument, so the public speed control is applied as one pitch-preserving FFmpeg tempo pass on the finished WAV after all sections are joined.
The engine performs no number normalisation, so digits are expanded to words before synthesis via a narrow per-family allow-list.
The recognised non-verbal tag set is exactly the engine's own _NONVERBAL_PATTERN; [cough], [breath] and [gasp] are not tags and render as noise.
The published 4-bit and 8-bit OmniVoice conversions use a custom row-wise scale layout the pinned MLX loader cannot read, so this bf16 checkpoint is the only supported tier.
Long scripts are split privately into sentence-safe sections using the same reference for every section, report section progress, and honour cancellation between sections.

commercial_decisions.decision: 25,000 characters is the ceiling this contract sells. It is a deliberate commercial boundary, not a technical limit and not a placeholder for a larger number.
commercial_decisions.context: The adapter's own request model caps text at 40,000 characters (app/backend/main.py:228), so the contract sits below what the code would accept. That headroom is intentional: the owner has considered a 40K tier and does not want one. No measurement is pending, and none is owed — a technical limit is not what this field records.

authoring_choices: adapter.version = 1.1 is an authoring choice — no adapter-version registry exists in code. 1.1 rather than 1.0 because the superseded record already published 1.0 against a different contract.
evidence.recorded_by: Contract authored and verified by the Voice Studio session against this repository's own code; owner verdicts and fleet-cache observations carried over from the GenStudio session's record, which was written concurrently at the owner's explicit direction and shipped as v1.32.8. Neither session's evidence was discarded: the quality judgements are the owner's, the contract fields are the code's.
